review_locator: PMCID:PMC3695728, Exploring mechanisms of FGF signalling through the lens of structural biology
primary_title: Crystal structures of two FGF-FGFR complexes reveal the determinants of ligand-receptor specificity
decision_basis: The review identifies the FGF1-FGFR1 structural receptor pair; the cited primary paper resolves the FGF1-FGFR1 ligand-binding complex and maps the receptor specificity interface.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the exact extracellular FGF1-FGFR1 structural binding/assembly layer; preserve heparan-sulfate and receptor-domain context and do not infer a universal FGFR1 cellular relay.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3695728, Exploring mechanisms of FGF signalling through the lens of structural biology
primary_title: Crystal structures of two FGF-FGFR complexes reveal the determinants of ligand-receptor specificity
decision_basis: The review identifies the FGF2-FGFR2 structural receptor pair; the cited primary paper resolves the FGF2-FGFR2 ligand-binding complex and maps receptor-specificity determinants.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the exact extracellular FGF2-FGFR2 structural binding/assembly layer; preserve receptor splice/heparan-sulfate context and do not infer an unqualified downstream FGFR2 pathway.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5647933, Lymphangiogenesis guidance by paracrine and pericellular factors; PMCID:PMC3385940, Signal Transduction by Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptors
primary_title: Structural and mechanistic insights into VEGF receptor 3 ligand binding and activation; A novel vascular endothelial growth factor, VEGF-C, is a ligand for the Flt4 (VEGFR-3) and KDR (VEGFR-2) receptor tyrosine kinases
decision_basis: The reviews identify mature VEGF-C as the primary VEGFR3 ligand; the cited primary studies resolve the VEGF-C/VEGFR3 ligand-binding interface and show receptor dimerization/activation, with the original ligand study demonstrating VEGFR3 autophosphorylation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve proteolytically processed/mature VEGF-C, FLT4/VEGFR3 D1-D7 topology and lymphatic-endothelial context; do not infer SCI vascular weighting.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5816233, Biology of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C in the Morphogenesis of Lymphatic Vessels; PMCID:PMC3385940, Signal Transduction by Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptors
primary_title: A novel vascular endothelial growth factor, VEGF-C, is a ligand for the Flt4 (VEGFR-3) and KDR (VEGFR-2) receptor tyrosine kinases; Structural determinants of growth factor binding and specificity by VEGF receptor 2
decision_basis: The reviews identify processed VEGF-C as a VEGFR2 ligand in addition to VEGFR3; the cited primary studies show VEGF-C binding/activation of KDR and resolve the VEGF-C/VEGFR2 D2-D3 interface.
limitations_preserved: Preserve proteolytic processing as a determinant of VEGFR2 binding/activation and distinguish KDR from FLT4; no SCI or endothelial-subtype extrapolation.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5816233, Biology of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C in the Morphogenesis of Lymphatic Vessels; PMCID:PMC3195192, An overview of lymphatic vessels and their emerging role in cardiovascular disease
primary_title: The specificity of receptor binding by vascular endothelial growth factor-d is different in mouse and man
decision_basis: The reviews identify VEGF-D as a VEGFR3 ligand; the cited primary study compares human and mouse VEGF-D receptor specificity and demonstrates binding/activation of VEGFR3 with species-dependent receptor usage.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human-versus-mouse VEGF-D specificity and proteolytically processed ligand form; do not collapse VEGFR3 and VEGFR2 branches or infer SCI relevance.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5816233, Biology of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C in the Morphogenesis of Lymphatic Vessels; PMCID:PMC3195192, An overview of lymphatic vessels and their emerging role in cardiovascular disease
primary_title: The specificity of receptor binding by vascular endothelial growth factor-d is different in mouse and man; Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-D and VEGF-A differentially regulate KDR-mediated signaling and biological function in vascular endothelial cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify VEGF-D as a ligand for VEGFR2; the cited primary studies demonstrate VEGF-D binding/activation of KDR and characterize downstream endothelial signaling and function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human/mouse ligand and processing/species boundaries, and distinguish VEGFD-KDR from VEGFD-FLT4; no SCI vascular claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2682371, Neuregulin 1 in neural development, synaptic plasticity and schizophrenia; PMCID:PMC109195, ErbB Tyrosine Kinases and the Two Neuregulin Families Constitute a Ligand-Receptor Network
primary_title: Direct Binding of the EGF-like Domain of Neuregulin-1 to Integrins Is Involved in Neuregulin-1/ErbB Signaling; Structures of the HER2-HER3-NRG1β complex reveal a dynamic dimer interface
decision_basis: The reviews identify ERBB3/HER3 as a direct NRG1 receptor; the cited primary study measures recombinant NRG1-ERBB3 binding and NRG1-dependent ERBB3 signaling, while the later structure resolves NRG1β bound in the HER2-HER3 complex.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NRG1 isoform/EGF-domain and ERBB3 direct-ligand context; ERBB2 is a coreceptor in the structural complex, and no neural/SCI receiver claim is made.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2682371, Neuregulin 1 in neural development, synaptic plasticity and schizophrenia; PMCID:PMC109195, ErbB Tyrosine Kinases and the Two Neuregulin Families Constitute a Ligand-Receptor Network
primary_title: Structures of the HER2-HER3-NRG1β complex reveal a dynamic dimer interface
decision_basis: The reviews describe NRG1-driven ErbB2/ErbB3 heterocomplex formation; the cited primary cryo-EM/structural study directly resolves the human HER2-HER3-NRG1β assembly and analyzes its dynamic singly liganded interface.
limitations_preserved: Promote only NRG1β-dependent HER2-HER3 extracellular complex assembly; preserve the singly liganded structural context and do not infer full-cell kinase activation from the structure alone.
